source.text: וַיְבָ֣רֶךְ אֱלֹהִ֔ים אֶת־נֹ֖חַ וְאֶת־בָּנָ֑יו וַיֹּ֧אמֶר לָהֶ֛ם פְּר֥וּ וּרְב֖וּ וּמִלְא֥וּ אֶת־הָאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: And blessed God Noah and his sons and said to them, be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth.

en.L: And God blessed Noah and his sons and said to them, "Be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth.
en.B: Then God blessed Noah and his sons and said to them, "Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the earth.
en.R: Then God blessed Noah and his sons. He said to them, "Have many children, so that there are more and more of you, and fill the earth.

es.L: Y bendijo Dios a Noé y a sus hijos, y les dijo: «{{plural_you:Sean|Sed}} fecundos y {{plural_you:multiplíquense|multiplicaos}}, y {{plural_you:llenen|llenad}} la tierra.
es.B: Entonces Dios bendijo a Noé y a sus hijos, y les dijo: «{{plural_you:Sean|Sed}} fecundos y {{plural_you:multiplíquense|multiplicaos}}, y {{plural_you:llenen|llenad}} la tierra.
es.R: Entonces Dios bendijo a Noé y a sus hijos. Les dijo: «{{plural_you:Tengan|Tened}} hijos, para que cada vez haya más de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, y {{plural_you:llenen|llenad}} la tierra.

fr.L: Et Dieu bénit Noé et ses fils et leur dit : « Soyez féconds et multipliez-vous, et remplissez la terre.
fr.B: Puis Dieu bénit Noé et ses fils et leur dit : « Soyez féconds, devenez nombreux et remplissez la terre.
fr.R: Ensuite, Dieu a béni Noé et ses fils. Il leur a dit : « Ayez beaucoup d’enfants, pour être de plus en plus nombreux, et remplissez la terre.

sw.L: Na Mungu akambariki Nuhu na wanawe, akawaambia, "Zaeni na mwongezeke na kuijaza dunia.
sw.B: Kisha Mungu akambariki Nuhu na wanawe, akawaambia, "Zaeni kwa wingi, mwongezeke na kuijaza dunia.
sw.R: Kisha Mungu akambariki Nuhu na wanawe. Akawaambia, "Zaeni watoto wengi, ili mzidi kuwa wengi, na mkaijaze dunia.

decisions.choice: be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth: the blessing of 1:28 renewed
decisions.reason: God gives Noah and his sons the blessing he gave the first human beings (1:28), word for word. Humankind begins again, with the same calling. The command to "subdue" the earth is not repeated.

decisions.choice: ustedes forms by default (Sean, multiplíquense, llenen, ustedes); vosotros forms with the setting (Sed, multiplicaos, llenad, vosotros)
decisions.reason: God speaks to Noah and his sons together, so every verb and pronoun of address is plural and carries a plural-you span, as in 1:28, whose wording verses 1 and 7 repeat (m1). "Les dijo" is the narrator's third person and has none. The same holds for God's speech to the end of verse 17.

decisions.choice: passé simple at Literal and Balanced ("bénit", "dit"); passé composé at Readable ("a béni", "a dit")
decisions.reason: As the French style guide sets out: the passé simple is the normal tense of written narrative, while Readable uses the passé composé, the tense of spoken French and of school reading. God's speech keeps the tenses of speech at every level.

source.text: וּמוֹרַאֲכֶ֤ם וְחִתְּכֶם֙ יִֽהְיֶ֔ה עַ֚ל כָּל־חַיַּ֣ת הָאָ֔רֶץ וְעַ֖ל כָּל־ע֣וֹף הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם בְּכֹל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר תִּרְמֹ֧שׂ הָֽאֲדָמָ֛ה וּֽבְכָל־דְּגֵ֥י הַיָּ֖ם בְּיֶדְכֶ֥ם נִתָּֽנוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] fear of you and [the] dread of you will be on every animal of the earth and on every bird of the heavens, on all that creeps [on] the ground and on all [the] fish of the sea; into your hand they are given.

en.L: And the fear of you and the dread of you will be on every animal of the earth and on every bird of the heavens, on everything that creeps on the ground and on all the fish of the sea; into your hand they are given.
en.B: Every animal on the earth, every bird of the sky, every creature that moves along the ground and all the fish of the sea will fear you and dread you. They are placed in your power.
en.R: All the animals, birds, small creatures and fish will be afraid of you. I am putting them under your control.

es.L: Y el temor de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} y el pavor de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} estarán sobre todos los animales de la tierra y sobre todas las aves de los cielos, sobre todo lo que se arrastra por el suelo y sobre todos los peces del mar; en la mano de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} son entregados.
es.B: Todos los animales de la tierra, todas las aves del cielo, todos los seres que se mueven por el suelo y todos los peces del mar sentirán temor y terror ante {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Quedan puestos en poder de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.R: Todos los animales, las aves, los animalitos y los peces {{plural_you:les|os}} tendrán miedo. Los pongo bajo el control de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.

fr.L: Et la crainte de vous et l’effroi de vous seront sur tout animal de la terre et sur tout oiseau des cieux, sur tout ce qui rampe sur le sol et sur tous les poissons de la mer ; ils sont livrés entre vos mains.
fr.B: Tous les animaux de la terre, tous les oiseaux du ciel, toutes les bêtes qui se déplacent sur le sol et tous les poissons de la mer vous craindront et auront peur de vous. Ils sont remis en votre pouvoir.
fr.R: Tous les animaux, les oiseaux, les petites bêtes et les poissons auront peur de vous. Je les mets sous votre autorité.

sw.L: Na hofu yenu na kitisho chenu vitakuwa juu ya kila mnyama wa dunia na juu ya kila ndege wa angani, juu ya kila kitambaacho ardhini na juu ya samaki wote wa baharini; wametiwa mkononi mwenu.
sw.B: Kila mnyama duniani, kila ndege wa angani, kila kiumbe kinachotambaa ardhini na samaki wote wa baharini watawaogopa na kuwahofu. Wamewekwa chini ya mamlaka yenu.
sw.R: Wanyama wote, ndege, viumbe vidogo na samaki watawaogopa. Ninawapa mamlaka juu yao.

decisions.choice: fear and dread of you: the relation between people and animals changes
decisions.reason: Humankind still rules the animals (1:26-28), but the relationship is no longer peaceful: animals will fear people, who will now kill them for food (verse 3). Isaiah looks forward to a time when this fear ends (Isaiah 11:6-9).

decisions.choice: into your hand they are given: placed in your power
decisions.reason: "Into your hand" means into your control, a phrase used of victory over enemies (Deuteronomy 20:13).

decisions.choice: en la mano de ustedes (L); en poder de ustedes (B); bajo el control de ustedes (R)
decisions.reason: With "ustedes" the possessive "su" can also mean "their", and here the animals are the subject, so "en su mano" could be read as the animals' own hand. Spanish says "de ustedes" to keep the sense of m2 clear; the setting gives "de vosotros".

source.text: כָּל־רֶ֨מֶשׂ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הוּא־חַ֔י לָכֶ֥ם יִהְיֶ֖ה לְאָכְלָ֑ה כְּיֶ֣רֶק עֵ֔שֶׂב נָתַ֥תִּי לָכֶ֖ם אֶת־כֹּֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: Every moving thing that is alive will be food for you; like [the] green plants I give you everything.

en.L: Every moving thing that is alive will be food for you; as [I gave] the green plants, I give you everything.
en.B: Every living thing that moves will be food for you. Just as I gave you the green plants, I now give you everything.
en.R: You may eat any animal that lives and moves. I gave you green plants to eat, and now I give you everything.

es.L: Todo lo que se mueve y tiene vida será alimento para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}; como [di] las plantas verdes, {{plural_you:les|os}} doy todo.
es.B: Todo ser vivo que se mueve {{plural_you:les|os}} servirá de alimento. Así como {{plural_you:les|os}} di las plantas verdes, ahora {{plural_you:les|os}} doy todo.
es.R: {{plural_you:Pueden|Podéis}} comer cualquier animal que vive y se mueve. {{plural_you:Les|Os}} di plantas verdes para comer, y ahora {{plural_you:les|os}} doy todo.

fr.L: Tout ce qui se meut et qui est vivant sera pour vous de la nourriture ; comme [je vous ai donné] les plantes vertes, je vous donne tout.
fr.B: Tout être vivant qui se meut vous servira de nourriture. Comme je vous ai donné les plantes vertes, désormais je vous donne tout.
fr.R: Vous pouvez manger tous les animaux qui vivent et qui bougent. Je vous avais donné les plantes vertes à manger ; maintenant, je vous donne tout.

sw.L: Kila kiendacho kilicho hai kitakuwa chakula kwenu; kama [nilivyowapa] mimea ya kijani, nawapa vyote.
sw.B: Kila kiumbe hai kinachotembea kitakuwa chakula chenu. Kama nilivyowapa mimea ya kijani, sasa nawapa vitu vyote.
sw.R: Mnaweza kula mnyama yeyote anayeishi na kutembea. Niliwapa mimea ya kijani mle, na sasa nawapa kila kitu.

decisions.choice: as the green plants, I give you everything: 1:29-30 widened
decisions.reason: In 1:29-30 God gave plants for food. Now he gives animals as well, with one limit (verse 4). The verb "I give" repeats 1:29.

decisions.choice: as [I gave] the green plants
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "like the green plants"; Literal brackets the words that make the comparison clear.

source.text: אַךְ־בָּשָׂ֕ר בְּנַפְשׁ֥וֹ דָמ֖וֹ לֹ֥א תֹאכֵֽלוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Only flesh with its life, its blood, you shall not eat.

en.L: But flesh with its life, its blood, you shall not eat.
en.B: But you must not eat meat that still has its lifeblood in it.
en.R: But you must not eat meat that still has blood in it, because the blood is its life.

es.L: Pero carne con su vida, su sangre, no {{plural_you:comerán|comeréis}}.
es.B: Pero no {{plural_you:deben|debéis}} comer la carne con su vida, es decir, con su sangre.
es.R: Pero no {{plural_you:deben|debéis}} comer carne que todavía tenga sangre, porque la sangre es su vida.

fr.L: Mais la chair avec sa vie, son sang, vous ne la mangerez pas.
fr.B: Mais vous ne mangerez pas une viande qui contient encore son sang, sa vie.
fr.R: Mais vous ne devez pas manger de viande où il y a encore du sang, parce que le sang, c’est la vie de l’animal.

sw.L: Lakini nyama pamoja na uhai wake, yaani damu yake, msile.
sw.B: Lakini msile nyama ambayo bado ina damu yake, yaani uhai wake.
sw.R: Lakini msile nyama ambayo bado ina damu, kwa sababu damu ndiyo uhai wake.

decisions.choice: flesh with its life, its blood: life belongs to God
decisions.reason: The blood is treated as the life of the creature, and life belongs to God who gives it. So blood is not to be eaten; it is poured out (Leviticus 17:10-14; Deuteronomy 12:23-24). The rule applies to all humankind, not only to Israel, and the early church kept it (Acts 15:20, 29).

decisions.choice: life: the word often translated soul
decisions.reason: The word (nefesh) is the life of a living creature, as in 1:20 and 2:7.

decisions.choice: its lifeblood
decisions.reason: Balanced joins "its life, its blood" into one word that says both.

decisions.choice: la carne con su vida, es decir, con su sangre
alternatives: la carne con su sangre vital
decisions.reason: English Balanced joins the two words into "lifeblood"; Spanish has no plain single word for it, so Balanced keeps both nouns and says that the blood is the life (m1, m2).

source.text: וְאַ֨ךְ אֶת־דִּמְכֶ֤ם לְנַפְשֹֽׁתֵיכֶם֙ אֶדְרֹ֔שׁ מִיַּ֥ד כָּל־חַיָּ֖ה אֶדְרְשֶׁ֑נּוּ וּמִיַּ֣ד הָֽאָדָ֗ם מִיַּד֙ אִ֣ישׁ אָחִ֔יו אֶדְרֹ֖שׁ אֶת־נֶ֥פֶשׁ הָֽאָדָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And surely your blood, for your lives, I will require; from [the] hand of every animal I will require it, and from [the] hand of humankind, from [the] hand of each man his brother I will require the life of humankind.

en.L: And surely for your lifeblood I will require a reckoning; from every animal I will require it, and from {{gender:humankind|man}}; from each one, for the life of {{gender:another|his brother}}, I will require the life of {{gender:a human being|man}}.
en.B: And for your lifeblood I will surely demand an accounting. I will demand it from every animal, and from every human being: from each person I will demand an accounting for the life of another.
en.R: If anyone takes a human life, I will hold them to account. If an animal kills a person, I will hold it to account. And if one person kills another, I will hold the killer to account.

es.L: Y ciertamente por la sangre de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, por {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} vidas, pediré cuentas; a todo animal se las pediré, y {{gender:al ser humano|al hombre}}; a cada uno, por la vida de {{gender:otro|su hermano}}, pediré cuentas de la vida {{gender:del ser humano|del hombre}}.
es.B: Y por la sangre de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, que es {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} vida, sin falta pediré cuentas. Se las pediré a todo animal y a todo ser humano: a cada persona le pediré cuentas por la vida de otra.
es.R: Si alguien quita una vida humana, le pediré cuentas. Si un animal mata a una persona, le pediré cuentas. Y si una persona mata a otra, le pediré cuentas al asesino.

fr.L: Et certes, de votre sang, de votre vie, je demanderai compte ; à tout animal j’en demanderai compte, et à {{gender:l’être humain|l’homme}} ; à chacun, pour la vie de {{gender:l’autre|son frère}}, je demanderai compte de la vie de {{gender:l’être humain|l’homme}}.
fr.B: Et de votre sang, qui est votre vie, je demanderai sûrement compte. J’en demanderai compte à tout animal et à tout être humain : à chacun je demanderai compte de la vie d’autrui.
fr.R: Si quelqu’un prend la vie d’un être humain, je lui en demanderai compte. Si un animal tue une personne, je lui en demanderai compte. Et si quelqu’un tue une autre personne, je demanderai compte au meurtrier.

sw.L: Na hakika damu yenu, kwa ajili ya uhai wenu, nitaidai; kutoka kwa kila mnyama nitaidai, na kutoka kwa mwanadamu; kutoka kwa kila mtu, kwa ajili ya uhai wa ndugu yake, nitadai uhai wa mwanadamu.
sw.B: Na kwa ajili ya damu yenu, yaani uhai wenu, hakika nitadai hesabu. Nitaidai kwa kila mnyama na kwa kila mwanadamu: kwa kila mtu nitadai hesabu ya uhai wa mwenzake.
sw.R: Mtu yeyote akiua mtu, nitamwajibisha. Mnyama akiua mtu, nitamwajibisha. Na mtu akimwua mwenzake, nitamwajibisha muuaji huyo.

decisions.choice: require: demand an accounting for
decisions.reason: The verb means to seek or to demand back. God will call to account whoever, animal or human, takes a human life (Exodus 21:28; Psalm 9:13).

decisions.choice: each one, his brother: every person, for another person
decisions.reason: "Each man ... his brother" is a Hebrew way of saying "one another". Every human being is the other's brother; murder is always the killing of a brother, as with Cain (4:8-11).

decisions.choice: each one ... another ... a human being; with the traditional setting, his brother, man
decisions.reason: The words mean every person, man or woman; the default is inclusive.

decisions.choice: pediré cuentas
decisions.reason: The verb means to demand an accounting (m1). "Pedir cuentas" says that in everyday Spanish at every level; "demandar" now suggests a lawsuit.

decisions.choice: por la sangre de ustedes, por sus vidas
alternatives: por la sangre de sus vidas
decisions.reason: English Literal merges blood and lives into "lifeblood". Spanish Literal keeps the two Hebrew phrases, "your blood" and "for your lives", each with a plural-you span.

decisions.choice: "ndugu yake", with no gender span
decisions.reason: Swahili "ndugu" means a brother or a sister, so Literal can keep the Hebrew "his brother" and still say "another person", with nothing for the gender setting to change.

source.text: שֹׁפֵךְ֙ דַּ֣ם הָֽאָדָ֔ם בָּֽאָדָ֖ם דָּמ֣וֹ יִשָּׁפֵ֑ךְ כִּ֚י בְּצֶ֣לֶם אֱלֹהִ֔ים עָשָׂ֖ה אֶת־הָאָדָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: [The one] shedding [the] blood of humankind, by humankind his blood will be shed; for in [the] image of God he made humankind.

en.L: Whoever sheds the blood of {{gender:a human being|man}}, by {{gender:a human being|man}} {{gender:that person's|his}} blood will be shed; for in the image of God {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made {{gender:humankind|man}}.
en.B: Whoever sheds human blood, by a human being that person's blood will be shed; for God made human beings in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own image.
en.R: Whoever kills a person must be put to death by others, because God made people to be like {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: El que derrame la sangre {{gender:del ser humano|del hombre}}, por {{gender:el ser humano|el hombre}} su sangre será derramada; porque a imagen de Dios hizo {{gender:a la humanidad|al hombre}}.
es.B: Quien derrame sangre humana, por un ser humano será derramada su sangre; porque Dios hizo a los seres humanos a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} propia imagen.
es.R: Quien mate a una persona deberá morir a manos de otros, porque Dios hizo a las personas para que se parecieran a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.

fr.L: Celui qui verse le sang de {{gender:l’être humain|l’homme}}, par {{gender:l’être humain|l’homme}} son sang sera versé ; car à l’image de Dieu {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a fait {{gender:l’être humain|l’homme}}.
fr.B: Quiconque verse le sang humain, par un être humain son sang sera versé ; car Dieu a fait les êtres humains à {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} propre image.
fr.R: Celui qui tue une personne devra être mis à mort par d’autres, parce que Dieu a fait les humains pour qu’ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ressemblent.

sw.L: Amwagaye damu ya mwanadamu, na mwanadamu damu yake itamwagwa; kwa maana katika sura ya Mungu {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} alimfanya mwanadamu.
sw.B: Yeyote amwagaye damu ya binadamu, damu yake itamwagwa na binadamu; kwa kuwa Mungu aliwafanya wanadamu kwa sura {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}}.
sw.R: Mtu akimwua mtu, lazima yeye pia auawe na watu, kwa sababu Mungu aliwaumba watu wafanane {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}.

decisions.choice: whoever sheds ... by a human being his blood will be shed: a poem of exact justice
alternatives: in exchange for the human, his blood will be shed
decisions.reason: The first line is poetry, its words in mirror order (sheds, blood, human / human, blood, shed). "By a human being" most likely means that the penalty is carried out by human hands, so that God gives humankind the duty of justice for murder. The small word can also mean "in exchange for": a life for a life.

decisions.choice: for in the image of God he made humankind: the reason human life is sacred
decisions.reason: Murder is an attack on God's own image (1:26-27). Even after the flood, and after all the evil of 6:5, every human being still bears the image of God.

decisions.choice: he made (Literal), his own image (Balanced), like him (Readable): deity pronoun setting
decisions.reason: Pronouns for God take the deity pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: del ser humano, el ser humano, a la humanidad; with the traditional setting, del hombre, el hombre, al hombre; "su sangre" with no span
decisions.reason: The gender spans follow 1:26-27, whose "a imagen de Dios" this verse repeats (m2). English needs a span for "that person's" / "his"; Spanish "su" is the same for either, so it has none. Balanced and Readable, like the English, say "ser humano" and "personas" with no span.

records.literal_gloss: And you, be fruitful and multiply, swarm on the earth and multiply on it.

en.L: And you, be fruitful and multiply, swarm on the earth and multiply on it."
en.B: As for you, be fruitful and multiply; spread over the earth and multiply on it."
en.R: As for you, have many children. Spread out over the earth and fill it."

es.L: Y {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, {{plural_you:sean|sed}} fecundos y {{plural_you:multiplíquense|multiplicaos}}; {{plural_you:pululen|pululad}} sobre la tierra y {{plural_you:multiplíquense|multiplicaos}} en ella».
es.B: En cuanto a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, {{plural_you:sean|sed}} fecundos y {{plural_you:multiplíquense|multiplicaos}}; {{plural_you:extiéndanse|extendeos}} por la tierra y {{plural_you:multiplíquense|multiplicaos}} en ella».
es.R: En cuanto a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, {{plural_you:tengan|tened}} muchos hijos. {{plural_you:Espárzanse|Esparcíos}} por la tierra y {{plural_you:llénenla|llenadla}}».

fr.L: Et vous, soyez féconds et multipliez-vous, pullulez sur la terre et multipliez-vous sur elle. »
fr.B: Quant à vous, soyez féconds et devenez nombreux ; répandez-vous sur la terre et multipliez-vous sur elle. »
fr.R: Et vous, ayez beaucoup d’enfants. Dispersez-vous sur la terre et remplissez-la. »

sw.L: Nanyi zaeni na mwongezeke, mjae tele duniani na mwongezeke ndani yake."
sw.B: Na ninyi, zaeni kwa wingi na mwongezeke; eneeni duniani na mwongezeke ndani yake."
sw.R: Na ninyi, zaeni watoto wengi. Eneeni duniani kote na kuijaza."

decisions.choice: be fruitful and multiply: the blessing repeated
decisions.reason: The speech ends as it began (verse 1): life, not death, is God's purpose. "Swarm" is the word used of the creatures in 1:20-21 and 8:17.

en.R: Then God said to Noah and his sons,

es.L: Y dijo Dios a Noé y a sus hijos con él:
es.B: Entonces Dios dijo a Noé y a sus hijos que estaban con él:
es.R: Entonces Dios les dijo a Noé y a sus hijos:

fr.L: Et Dieu dit à Noé et à ses fils avec lui :
fr.B: Puis Dieu dit à Noé et à ses fils qui étaient avec lui :
fr.R: Ensuite, Dieu a dit à Noé et à ses fils :

sw.L: Na Mungu akamwambia Nuhu na wanawe pamoja naye, akisema,

decisions.choice: my covenant: the covenant promised in 6:18
decisions.reason: God now sets up the covenant he promised Noah before the flood. It is God's own covenant: he makes it and binds himself by it, and asks nothing in return.

decisions.choice: your offspring after you: all future generations
decisions.reason: The covenant includes all of Noah's descendants, that is, all humankind.

decisions.choice: be cut off: be destroyed
decisions.reason: "Cut off" means destroyed or wiped out. It is also the verb used for making a covenant ("cutting" a covenant, 15:18); the promise is that life will not be cut off.

decisions.choice: never again a flood to destroy the earth: God's unconditional promise
decisions.reason: God binds himself, without conditions, never to destroy all life by a flood again (8:21). The promise does not depend on human goodness.

decisions.choice: será exterminada
decisions.reason: The verb means cut off, that is, wiped out (m1). Spanish "cortar" does not carry that sense, so even Literal says "exterminada"; the link with "cutting" a covenant is left to m1.

decisions.choice: pacto (verses 11-17)
decisions.reason: English Readable says "promise" from here on, because "covenant" is a hard word in English. Spanish "pacto" is a plain word that young readers know (see 6:18), so Readable keeps "pacto" throughout, as Literal and Balanced do.

decisions.choice: "alliance" at Readable too (verses 11-17)
decisions.reason: "L'alliance" is the settled term for God's covenant, and the same word runs through verses 9-17 and on to Abraham and Sinai. It is a common French word, so Readable keeps it where the English Readable says "promise", as the Spanish keeps "pacto".

decisions.choice: "agano" at Readable too (verses 11-17)
decisions.reason: "Agano" is the settled term for God's covenant and an everyday Swahili word for a binding agreement, so Readable keeps it where the English Readable says "promise"; the same word then runs through verses 9-17.

decisions.choice: sign of the covenant: a visible token of the promise
decisions.reason: A sign is something that can be seen and that points to something else. Each of God's covenants in Genesis and Exodus has one: the bow here, circumcision with Abraham (17:11), the Sabbath at Sinai (Exodus 31:13).

decisions.choice: for generations forever: for all time
decisions.reason: "For everlasting generations" means without end.

decisions.choice: entre yo y ustedes (L); con ustedes (B); the same in verses 13, 15 and 17
decisions.reason: After "entre" modern Spanish uses "yo", not "mí"; "entre mí y vosotros" is the older Bible phrasing. Literal keeps God first, as in the Hebrew; Balanced says "con", or puts "yo" last ("entre la tierra y yo", verse 13), as natural Spanish does. Spanish writes "yo" without a deity-pronoun span, as English does with "I".

decisions.choice: my bow: the rainbow, called by the word for a warrior's bow
alternatives: only the rainbow, with no further sense
decisions.reason: The word is the ordinary word for a bow used in war or hunting. God calls the rainbow "my bow". Many readers see in it a picture of God setting aside his weapon of judgment, hanging up his bow; the text itself says only that it is the sign of the covenant.

decisions.choice: I have set: a gift made as God speaks
alternatives: I set (in the past, at creation)
decisions.reason: The completed verb form is used, as in 1:29, for an act done by the words that announce it: God now appoints the bow as the sign.

decisions.choice: rainbow
decisions.reason: Readable says "rainbow", which is what the bow is, so that young readers do not picture a weapon; the sense of the warrior's bow is explained in m1.

decisions.choice: mi arco (L, B); mi arcoíris (R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep "arco", the plain word for a bow, as the Hebrew and English do (m1); in this setting a Spanish reader still sees the rainbow. Readable says "arcoíris", the spelling now preferred to "arco iris".

decisions.choice: I will remember: I will act on my promise
decisions.reason: As in 8:1, God's remembering means acting faithfully on his commitment, not recalling something he had forgotten. The sign is for God as well as for people: when he sees it, he keeps his word.

decisions.choice: everlasting covenant: a covenant without end

decisions.choice: between God and every living creature: God speaks of himself by name
decisions.reason: God speaks of himself as "God", as rulers and judges sometimes did, which makes the promise sound like a solemn legal statement.

decisions.reason: "The whole earth" means all the people of the earth (as in 11:1). Chapter 10 lists the peoples who came from the three sons.

records.literal_gloss: And began Noah, the man of the ground, and he planted a vineyard.

en.L: And Noah, a man of the ground, began [farming] and planted a vineyard.
en.B: Noah, a man of the soil, was the first to plant a vineyard.
en.R: Noah was a farmer. He was the first person to plant a vineyard.

es.L: Y Noé, hombre del suelo, comenzó [a labrar] y plantó una viña.
es.B: Noé, un hombre que labraba el suelo, fue el primero en plantar una viña.
es.R: Noé era agricultor. Fue la primera persona que plantó una viña.

decisions.choice: Noah, a man of the soil, began: he was the first to plant a vineyard
alternatives: Noah began to be a farmer
decisions.reason: The verb "began" can go with "man of the soil" (he began to farm) or with "planted" (he was the first to plant a vineyard). The second fits the stories of first things in these chapters (4:20-22, 26). "Man of the soil" recalls Lamech's hope for relief from the ground (5:29).

decisions.choice: began [farming]
decisions.reason: Literal brackets an object for "began", which has none in the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: un hombre que labraba el suelo
decisions.reason: "Hombre del suelo" (Literal) is not idiomatic Spanish; Balanced says what it means, keeping "suelo" for the ground as in chapters 2-8. "Hombre del campo" would suggest a countryman rather than one who works the soil.

source.text: וַיֵּ֥שְׁתְּ מִן־הַיַּ֖יִן וַיִּשְׁכָּ֑ר וַיִּתְגַּ֖ל בְּת֥וֹךְ אָהֳלֹֽה׃

es.L: Y bebió del vino y se emborrachó, y se quedó descubierto en el interior de su tienda.
es.B: Al beber de aquel vino, se emborrachó y quedó acostado, descubierto, dentro de su tienda.
es.R: Bebió del vino que había hecho y se emborrachó. Luego se quedó acostado y desnudo en su tienda.

decisions.choice: became drunk: the righteous man's failure
decisions.reason: Noah, called righteous and blameless (6:9), fails after the flood. The text reports it without excuse. Scripture elsewhere warns against drunkenness and the shame it brings (Proverbs 20:1; 23:29-35; Habakkuk 2:15).

decisions.choice: uncovered himself: lay exposed
decisions.reason: The verb means to uncover or expose oneself; in his drunkenness Noah lies naked.

en.R: Ham, the father of Canaan, saw his father lying naked. He went outside and told his two brothers about it.

es.L: Y Cam, el padre de Canaán, vio la desnudez de su padre y avisó a sus dos hermanos afuera.
es.B: Cam, el padre de Canaán, vio a su padre desnudo y salió a contárselo a sus dos hermanos.
es.R: Cam, el padre de Canaán, vio a su padre acostado y desnudo. Salió de la tienda y se lo contó a sus dos hermanos.

decisions.choice: saw his father's nakedness: looked on his father's shame
alternatives: a sexual act against Noah (or Noah's wife)
decisions.reason: "To see the nakedness" of someone can be a way of speaking of sexual relations (Leviticus 20:17), and some take it so here. But the next verse answers it exactly with covering and not seeing, which suggests that the wrong was Ham's looking on and telling, disgracing his father instead of covering his shame.

records.literal_gloss: And took Shem and Japheth the garment and put [it] on [the] shoulder of both of them and walked backward and covered the nakedness of their father, and their faces [were] backward, and the nakedness of their father they did not see.

en.L: And Shem and Japheth took the garment and laid it on both their shoulders, and walked backward and covered their father's nakedness; their faces [were turned] backward, and they did not see their father's nakedness.
en.B: But Shem and Japheth took a garment, laid it across their shoulders and walked in backward to cover their father's nakedness. Their faces were turned away, so they did not see their father naked.

es.L: Y tomaron Sem y Jafet el manto y lo pusieron sobre los hombros de ambos, y caminaron hacia atrás y cubrieron la desnudez de su padre; y sus rostros [estaban vueltos] hacia atrás, y no vieron la desnudez de su padre.
es.B: Pero Sem y Jafet tomaron un manto, se lo echaron sobre los hombros y entraron de espaldas para cubrir la desnudez de su padre. Tenían el rostro vuelto hacia otro lado, y así no vieron a su padre desnudo.
es.R: Pero Sem y Jafet tomaron una capa y la sostuvieron sobre sus hombros. Entraron de espaldas en la tienda y cubrieron a su padre. Mantuvieron la cara vuelta hacia otro lado para no verlo desnudo.

decisions.choice: covered ... did not see: honoring their father
decisions.reason: The brothers do the opposite of Ham: they cover what he looked on, and they do not see. Covering another's shame is a mark of love (Proverbs 10:12; 1 Peter 4:8). They honor their father as the later commandment requires (Exodus 20:12).

source.text: וַיִּ֥יקֶץ נֹ֖חַ מִיֵּינ֑וֹ וַיֵּ֕דַע אֵ֛ת אֲשֶׁר־עָ֥שָׂה־ל֖וֹ בְּנ֥וֹ הַקָּטָֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And awoke Noah from his wine and knew what had done to him his son the youngest.

en.L: And Noah awoke from his wine and knew what his youngest son had done to him.
en.B: When Noah awoke from his wine and found out what his youngest son had done to him,
en.R: When Noah woke up and was sober again, he found out what his youngest son had done to him.

es.L: Y despertó Noé de su vino y se enteró de lo que le había hecho su hijo menor.
es.B: Cuando Noé despertó de su borrachera y supo lo que le había hecho su hijo menor,
es.R: Cuando Noé despertó y ya no estaba borracho, se enteró de lo que le había hecho su hijo menor.

decisions.choice: his youngest son: Ham, the youngest
decisions.reason: The word means small or young; with the article it usually means the youngest. Ham is listed second (5:32; 9:18), so the list is not in order of birth. Some take "son" to mean grandson, Canaan, who is cursed next.

decisions.choice: despertó de su borrachera
decisions.reason: "Despertar de su vino" is the Hebrew idiom, kept at Literal; Balanced says it plainly, as English "awoke from his wine" can be understood but Spanish cannot.

source.text: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אָר֣וּר כְּנָ֑עַן עֶ֥בֶד עֲבָדִ֖ים יִֽהְיֶ֥ה לְאֶחָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said, cursed [be] Canaan; a slave of slaves he will be to his brothers.

en.L: And he said, "Cursed [be] Canaan; a slave of slaves he will be to his brothers."
en.B: he said, "Cursed be Canaan! He will be the lowest of servants to his brothers."
en.R: He said, "May there be a curse on Canaan! He will be the lowest servant of his brothers."

es.L: Y dijo: «Maldito [sea] Canaán; esclavo de esclavos será para sus hermanos».
es.B: dijo: «¡Maldito sea Canaán! Será el más bajo de los siervos para sus hermanos».
es.R: Entonces dijo: «¡Que caiga una maldición sobre Canaán! Será el más bajo de los sirvientes de sus hermanos».

decisions.choice: cursed be Canaan: Noah curses Ham's son, not Ham
decisions.reason: Noah's words are a prophetic curse on Canaan, Ham's son. The text does not explain why Canaan rather than Ham is named; it looks ahead to the Canaanites, whose land Israel later took and whose practices the law condemns (Leviticus 18:3, 24-28). The words are Noah's, not God's.

decisions.choice: the misuse of this verse: it names Canaan, not any race
decisions.reason: In modern times this verse was wrongly used to justify the enslavement of Africans, under the false idea of a "curse of Ham". The text curses Canaan only. It says nothing about skin color or race, and Canaan's descendants lived in the land of Canaan (10:15-19), not in Africa.

decisions.choice: a slave of slaves: the lowest of slaves
decisions.reason: Repeating a noun this way expresses the extreme ("song of songs", "holy of holies"). The word is the ordinary word for a slave.

decisions.choice: the lowest of servants
decisions.reason: "The lowest of servants" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; Literal keeps "a slave of slaves", and the meaning decision (m3) keeps the sense. The curse is that Canaan will be subject to his brothers, as Esau's line is to Jacob's in 27:37, where the word is also rendered with "serve".

decisions.choice: el más bajo de los siervos (B), de los sirvientes (R)
alternatives: el más bajo de los esclavos
decisions.reason: As in English, Balanced and Readable say "siervo"/"sirviente" for a curse of subjection (m3); Literal keeps "esclavo de esclavos". Readable uses "sirvientes", as in 12:5 (r-es-1).

decisions.choice: blessed be the LORD, the God of Shem: Shem's blessing is his God
decisions.reason: Instead of blessing Shem directly, Noah blesses the LORD as Shem's God. The line of Shem leads to Abraham (11:10-26) and to Israel, the people who will know God by this name.

decisions.choice: his slave: the slave of Shem (or of Shem's people)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew pronoun can be singular or plural ("to him" or "to them"); it refers to Shem, or to Shem and his descendants.

decisions.choice: Shem's servant
decisions.reason: Readable names Shem so that "his" is not taken to mean God's (m2).

decisions.choice: "el SEÑOR"; with the divine name setting, "Yahvé"
decisions.reason: As in 2:4: the default writes the name as SEÑOR in small capitals; the setting gives "Yahvé". The span takes in the article.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable (style guide); Literal keeps "slave".

decisions.choice: enlarge Japheth: a play on his name
decisions.reason: "May he enlarge" (yaft) sounds like the name Japheth (Yefet). Noah prays that Japheth's descendants will have room to spread, as the many peoples of 10:2-5 do.

decisions.choice: let him dwell in the tents of Shem: Japheth sharing in Shem's blessing
alternatives: let God dwell in the tents of Shem
decisions.reason: "He" most likely means Japheth: he will live peacefully with Shem and share in his blessing. Some read "he" as God, who will dwell among Shem's people. The verse does not decide.

decisions.choice: May Japheth live peacefully with Shem's people
alternatives: let him dwell in the tents of Shem
decisions.reason: Readable takes "he" as Japheth (m2) and explains the picture of sharing tents.

decisions.choice: ensanche
decisions.reason: The verb means to make room or space (m1); "ensanchar" says that, where "engrandecer" means to make great. The play on the name Japheth cannot be kept in Spanish and is explained in m1.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable (style guide); Literal keeps "slave".
